data.title: Coordinated Harassment of Named Staff
data.summary:
Named employees were subjected to coordinated abuse, including contact through personal
channels and publication of personal information, as a component of the campaign.
data.description:
Harassment of individuals is the point at which an influence operation produces direct
harm to people, and it is frequently the component the organisation is least prepared
for. Communications teams are equipped to handle reputational attack; they are not
equipped to support an employee whose home address has been published.

The operational objective is usually suppression: removing an inconvenient voice by making
participation personally costly. It is effective, and the resulting silence is sometimes
mistaken internally for the problem having subsided.

This finding is about identifiable people. They should be informed before it circulates,
their wishes should shape how it is written, and the duty of care sits above the
analytical interest in documenting it.
data.recommendation:
* Inform affected individuals before the report circulates and let their wishes shape how
  the finding is recorded.
* Provide practical support — personal data removal, platform escalation, security advice
  at home — rather than communications advice.
* Make clear that withdrawing from public channels is a supported option and not a failure.
* Preserve evidence for law enforcement where the conduct is criminal, and support any
  individual who wishes to report it.
data.short_recommendation: Support the individuals first; preserve evidence for law enforcement.
